fractions-meaning.title: What a fraction means
fractions-meaning.objective: Read a fraction as a number of equal parts out of a whole.

fractions-equivalence.title: Equivalent fractions
fractions-equivalence.objective: Explain and produce equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same number.

items.prompt: Is 1/2 equal to 2/4? Answer yes or no.
A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices and you eat 1. What fraction did you eat?
A bar has 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
In the fraction 5/7, how many equal parts is the whole split into?
Is 2/5 equal to 4/10? Answer yes or no.

steps: A fraction describes equal parts of one whole.
The bottom number (denominator) says how many equal parts the whole is split into.
The top number (numerator) says how many of those parts we are talking about.
So 1/4 means: split the whole into 4 equal parts and take 1 of them.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount using different numbers. If you multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number, the amount stays the same: 1/2 = (1x2)/(2x2) = 2/4.
Step 1: Picture 1/2 - one of two equal halves.
Step 2: Now cut each half into 2 smaller equal pieces. The whole now has 4 pieces.
Step 3: The half you had is now 2 of those 4 pieces, so it is 2/4.
Step 4: You cut every piece into 2, so both numbers were multiplied by 2. The amount did not change.

interest_templates.cooking: A recipe needs 1/2 cup of milk, but you only have a 1/4-cup measure. Two 1/4 cups fill the same amount as 1/2 cup, so 1/2 = 2/4.
interest_templates.sports: A match has 2 halves. Playing 1 half is the same as playing 2 of 4 quarters, so 1/2 = 2/4.
interest_templates.music: One half note lasts as long as two quarter notes, so 1/2 = 2/4.

relevant_example.fallback: Sharing a sandwich: half a sandwich is the same amount as 2 quarters of that sandwich, so 1/2 = 2/4.
steps: Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number keeps the amount the same.
This is practice, not a test - mistakes are useful information.
Hint: compare the two denominators first. What number turns one into the other?
Then do the same thing to the numerator.
